<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is being evaluated for safety when running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. These commands source the PKGBUILD, execute any code in the global scope and `pkgver()` function (if present), and fetch sources defined in the `source` array.

In this file, the `source` array contains only static HTTPS URLs pointing to trusted domains: `dist.torproject.org`, and commented alternatives from `mullvad.net` and `tor.eff.org`. These are legitimate sources for the Mullvad Browser. The files to be downloaded are a tarball and its signature, along with two local files (`mullvad-browser.sh`, `mullvad-browser.desktop`). No command substitution, dynamic URL generation, or untrusted network requests are present in the `source` array.

There is no `pkgver()` function defined, so no dynamic version computation occurs. The rest of the code outside `package()` consists only of static variable assignments (e.g., `pkgname`, `depends`, `sha256sums`). There is no execution of external commands, no use of command substitution (like `$(...)` or backticks), and no network activity triggered during sourcing. The PGP key listed in `validpgpkeys` is the official Tor Browser Developers key, which is appropriate.

Although the checksum for the `.asc` file is set to `SKIP`, this is not a concern for this safety gate, as unverified downloads are part of the intended workflow — the sources are fetched so they can be audited. Extraction happens after sourcing, and no code runs at this stage due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`.

Thus, sourcing this PKGBUILD and downloading the sources poses no risk of remote code execution or data exfiltration.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No dynamic code or unsafe sourcing; only static, trusted sources.
</summary>

LLM auditresponse for mullvad-browser.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The script is a simple wrapper to launch the Mullvad Browser with custom environment settings and optional user-defined flags. It respects standard XDG base directory conventions by using `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or falling back to `$HOME/.config`. It reads user flags from a configuration file if present, strips comments, and passes them to the browser executable.

The environment settings are security-conscious: disabling Nvidia shader disk caching reduces unwanted disk footprint and potential tracking, and `FONTCONFIG_PATH` is set to a bundled directory to ensure consistent font rendering without relying on system fonts. The `SESSION_MANAGER` is unset to prevent unintended session tracking, which is a known hardening technique in privacy-focused browsers.

All operations are self-contained, with no network calls, file exfiltration, or execution of external scripts. The `exec` call runs the locally installed browser binary with user-supplied arguments, which is expected behavior. There is no obfuscation, suspicious command usage, or deviation from standard packaging practices.
</details>
